item.content:encoded:
🚀 Headlines & Launches

Gemini 4 Hydrogen · 14 minute read

Google introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast, efficient model optimized for coding and agentic workflows. It scored 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, surpassing Gemini 4 Argon, and is priced at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.

Operate Claude Managed Agents inside your security perimeter · 4 minute read

Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents offers private beta for developers to build and run agents directly within their company's own infrastructure. This setup allows for a complete in-house deployment of the Managed Agents' services, including sandboxes, credential handling, and session history. Organizations benefit from enhanced security and control over agent operations, with the ability to integrate with existing cloud providers and comply with zero data retention policies.

Replit Agent can now buy for your business and help you reach customers · 5 minute read

Replit Agent now helps businesses with supply purchases and running Google Ads. It leverages Link with Visa and Stripe for secure, controlled transactions and simplifies ad campaigns by analyzing content and suggesting strategies.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

Top Chinese Frontier AI Models Carry the Fingerprint of Export-Controlled NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs · 37 minute read

A forensic analysis of publicly released AI models found evidence that DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group have gained access to Nvidia's Blackwell GPUs. Six models released by these companies since April contain numerical patterns that match Blackwell hardware. Several leading Chinese AI developers have likely begun using Blackwell to train their newest models. While the analysis provides technical evidence of access to advanced computing hardware, it doesn't establish where the chips were located, how access was obtained, or whether export controls were violated.

Eliminating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference with Integer-Only Arithmetic · 15 minute read

A floating-point number stores a fixed number of significant digits and a separate exponent. When two numbers with very different exponents are added, the small one has to be shifted to line up with the big one, and the digits that fall off on the end are gone. That means that (a+b)+c is not always equal to a+(b+c). This post looks at what happens when integer addition, which is exact, is used.

How Agent Anomaly Detection scores on benchmarks we didn't write · 8 minute read

Agent Anomaly Detection, tested against external benchmarks, flagged 87% of executed harmful instructions, highlighting strengths in identifying goal hijack and tool misuse but weaknesses with poisoned memory. It demonstrated varying false alarm rates, with the highest at 16% for tasks involving high-impact tools. Ongoing improvements focus on detecting small, potentially harmful actions, distinguishing normal use from misuse, and providing quicker full coverage for new agents.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Become a founding member of TLDR's AI community · 2 minute form

TLDR is launching a curated community for AI builders to discuss major news and launches. The best links and comments will be featured in TLDR AI. Apply here to join.

Atlas · Website

Atlas is an omni model that natively operates on text, images, video, and 3D. All inputs are combined into a shared spatial context. Atlas can perform a broad range of tasks spanning world generation, reconstruction, and simulation. Examples of scenes generated with the model are available.

Perplexity Decider · 26 minute read

Perplexity has released updates to two models inspired by Jev, TypeSafe AI's System One model. Perplexity Decider supports binary and multi-class classification with ordered or unordered labels. It returns probabilities that applications can use to classify, route, rank, and evaluate inputs. Both new models, Decider v1.3 and Decider Flash v1.3, improve performance and robustness across a broad range of text and vision tasks. They also have a new feature that highlights selected content for named entity recognition, personal information identification, and extractive question-answering tasks.

🎁 Miscellaneous

NVIDIA Announces CEO Transition · 3 minute read

Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia's CEO. Finance chief Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO until a permanent successor is named. The board is considering both internal and external candidates. Nvidia's board has appointed long-time director Harvey C. Jones as its first ever chair. The company will report its third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on November 17 as previously scheduled.

Everyone is learning the wrong lesson from Hugging Face · 9 minute read

The Hugging Face incident is commonly viewed as a cybersecurity incident. People see it as an example of how AI could be used to break into critical infrastructure and cause enormous damage. However, this isn't anything new: we have known about AI's hacking capabilities for a while. The real lesson is that frontier AIs want things we don't intend, and they will pursue those wants relentlessly.

⚡️ Quick Links

Orienting to 1 year AGI timelines · 22 minute read

Timelines to artificial superintelligence are now very short, with some predicting that it will be achieved within the next two years.

Use Claude Meetings · 4 minute read

Claude can now be added to Google Meet as a visible participant to take notes, answer questions, and build artifacts live during the call.

Fast by Default: Compile-Time Heuristics for Helion Kernels · 15 minute read

Helion's new compile-time heuristics boost kernel performance significantly without the need for time-consuming autotuning.

LiquidCodec: High-Fidelity Audio Tokenization Optimized for Speed · 17 minute read

LiquidCodec features fast speech generation with a small memory footprint, making it easier to build applications that can sustain a conversation while running locally.

Meta's Muse Can Now Call Businesses · 1 minute read

Meta expanded Muse's AI-powered calling feature to all paid subscribers, letting the assistant contact US businesses on users' behalf.

item.content:encoded:
🚀 Headlines & Launches

Gemini Decisions API: Fast, calibrated multimodal decisions · 1 minute read

Google's Gemini Decisions API enables fast, calibrated multimodal decision-making by analyzing inputs like images and text. It assesses scenarios and provides actionable insights, such as determining spill severity and recommending cleanup actions.

What's new in Grok Bot 1.0 · 11 minute read

Grok Bot 1.0 adds Team Bots you can publish and share, Slack and Microsoft Teams, meetings on Meet and Zoom, shared connectors, and reviewed learnings. It is now a personal assistant that the whole team can talk to in the app, in Slack, in Microsoft Teams, and in video calls. This post covers how to create a Team Bot and publish it, how to bring the bot into Microsoft Teams, how to add a bot to a meeting, and more. It also looks at the new admin controls and what's possible without a team.

Runway Praxis-1 Is Now Available: Open-Weight Robotics Model · 3 minute read

Runway's Praxis-1, a 27B-parameter open-weight robotics model, is now available under Apache 2.0. The model excels in predicting video and actions, topping NVIDIA's RoboLab-120 leaderboard with a 46.2% success rate across 1,200 episodes. It's accessible on GitHub and Hugging Face, with support for full and LoRA fine-tuning, compatible with NVIDIA hardware, and adaptable for various robotic embodiments.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

Escaping SPACE: Part II · 28 minute read

Perplexity tested 12 models against its SPACE agent sandbox: none escaped VM-host isolation, but several bypassed network controls through DNS spoofing and shared-IP exploitation before the flaws were fixed. The experiments also found that capture-the-flag prompts distracted agents from the security boundary being tested.

MCP vs CLI vs Skills: What Each Costs in Context · 11 minute read

MCP servers significantly increase token use, adding thousands of input tokens per request, unlike CLI or skill methods. On Sonnet 5.5, a simple task showed MCP consuming 59,417 tokens with default tools against CLI's 1,421 and skill's 3,315, highlighting the high cost of tool-heavy MCP setups. Implementing Tool Search can cut token costs by deferring tool definitions, reducing upfront toolset costs to under 600 tokens for optimal efficiency.

LLMs can learn some multi-step reasoning on filler tokens instead of visible CoT · 9 minute read

By changing the training setup and applying LoRAs to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and gpt-oss-20b, researchers taught models to do some multi-step tasks while emitting only filler tokens, beating an answer-only baseline on three of seven tasks. They also mapped theoretical layer-depth limits and showed empirical walls, with some tasks learned out to 60 steps and others failing after one to three. The work is meant to separate filler-token reasoning from steganographic hidden reasoning when interpreting chain-of-thought.

Don't Write Kernels, Derive Them · 63 minute read

Current models rely on hand-written kernels specific to operators, chips, and fusions, limiting flexibility across devices and scenarios. Tang's IR enables on-the-fly derivation of kernels through constructs such as views and comprehensions, eliminating the need for pre-defined kernels.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

AlphaGenome 2: Predicting how DNA shapes cells and disease · 9 minute read

AlphaGenome 2 improves prediction of DNA variant effects on specific cell types, aiding in disease understanding and research. It doubles variant identification compared to its predecessor and adapts to analyze new cell states without retraining. Available for non-commercial use, the tool bridges genetics and cell biology, pinpointing disease-relevant genetic mutations in primary human cells.

OpenAI open-sources MCP Extensions for ChatGPT-native plugins · 1 minute read

The TypeScript and Python packages add ChatGPT-specific features to MCP servers and apps, including sidebar entry points, custom file viewers, composer resource search, and thumbnail part pickers. The SDKs ship with a Bits & Bolts demo plugin and a written spec.

A2UI 1.0: Build delightful, fast, reliable, agentic experiences · 11 minute read

A2UI is an open protocol for generative UI that lets agents answer with interactive screens. Open-source renderer SDKs are now available for the web, Android, iOS, and agent SDKs for Python, TypeScript, and Dart. A2UI enables apps to draw UIs with native components, securely. Users get the same low latency, high trust, and complete native fidelity whether they reach a company's agent in its own app or in a third-party AI assistant that hosts MCP apps.

Shopify's generative discovery model · 14 minute read

Shopify deployed a shared generative discovery model for search and recommendation, leveraging semantic-ID tokens to enhance product personalization and relevance. The model improved online and offline metrics, such as a 9.85% lift in conversion rate and significant gains in search relevance.

Browser use has been rolling out in Antigravity · 1 minute read

Browser use in Antigravity closes the loop between researching, writing code, and verifying it live. Users control authentication, and downloads pause until they are approved. Agents can use the browser to run multiple tasks at once. A video demo is available in the post.

🎁 Miscellaneous

United moves to block AI agents · 2 minute read

United Airlines is moving to restrict AI-agent access across its platforms and agency channels, citing credential security and liability risks around tasks such as check-in. The restrictions contrast with travel companies including Expedia and Booking that are partnering with agents.

Why Connections Matter More in AI · 5 minute read

Professional relationships are becoming increasingly important in AI as coding agents commoditize technical execution, frontier research demands more compute resources, and closed-source development makes individual contributions harder to evaluate.

⚡️ Quick Links

Google Tabletop Creates Shared Interactive Planning Spaces · 1 minute read

Google Labs' Tabletop turns links, files, and prompts into interactive itineraries, polls, expense splitters, and tournament brackets.

ElevenAI · Website

ElevenAI is a desktop app that helps amplify work using agents.

OpenAI wants agents to tell websites where you are · 5 minute read

Two OpenAI engineers recently shared a proposal that suggests a change that will let agents pass user information along to websites to make them look like normal visitors rather than bots.

Nvidia board reportedly preparing to oust Huang · 3 minute read

Nvidia's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang following his admission of an affair with a woman US intelligence agencies believe was recruited by Chinese intelligence.

Airbnb's AI assistant cut support cost per booking 17% · 1 minute read

Airbnb's AI assistant cut support cost per booking by more than 17%, resolving about 40% of Q3 issues with no human agent.

Databricks Genie Agents · 13 minute read

Databricks Genie Agents can now analyze unstructured documents alongside database tables, connect to enterprise tools, and share insights externally with governance controls.

item.content:encoded:
🚀 Headlines & Launches

Working with Claude Sheets, Whiteboards, and Interactive Connectors · 5 minute read

Anthropic introduced Claude Sheets, Whiteboards, and Data, new artifact types that let teams build spreadsheets, organize ideas, and create dashboards with Claude without switching apps. Interactive connectors now embed partner apps like Adobe and Atlassian directly in Claude, and plugins from Salesforce, NetSuite, and Workday (in beta) ship with built-in skills for sales, finance, and HR work. Claude Meetings, which will bring Claude into calls to take notes and update documents, is coming soon.

Businesses and Business Agents in ChatGPT · 3 minute read

OpenAI introduced Businesses in ChatGPT, allowing companies to claim their profiles, update business information, provide product feeds with pricing and availability, and track customer engagement. Eligible e-commerce and online service businesses in the US can also launch Business Agents that answer questions and help customers explore their offerings inside ChatGPT. The launch is in beta.

Gemini 4 Carbon is now available · 12 minute read

Google's strongest model is now available to all paying developers and enterprises through the API in AI Studio and Gemini for business, and is rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Antigravity, the Gemini app, and AI Mode in Search. Google says Carbon ranks first on CursorBench 4.0, Perplexity's WANDR, and Zapier's AutomationBench at more than 2x lower cost per task than the next best external model, at the same $2/$10 per million input/output token price as Gemini 4 Argon. The release adds frontier cybersecurity capabilities through the Fairwind Program and previews /swarm, a multi-agent mode in Antigravity.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

Suppressing Reward Hacking Through Model Weight Arithmetic · 3 minute read

Researchers subtract code models trained with loose and strict rewards to identify a direction controlling inefficient solutions. Extrapolating beyond the strict model reduced resource-limit failures from 14.5% to 8% without additional training, though excessive extrapolation breaks outputs and stricter rewards can hurt correctness.

Why Instinct Feels Like a Personal Assistant · 20 minute read

A twelve-week analysis of one Instinct conversation attributes its appeal to short messages, quick acknowledgments, proactive follow-ups, and approval checks before purchases or outreach. The teardown suggests coordinated task agents and persistent memory underpin the experience, while exposing retention and delivery-verification failures.

Neurons as an Interpretable Basis · 15 minute read

Goodfire argues that individual language-model neurons are more interpretable than commonly assumed. Its Neuron Scientist agents generate and test descriptions of neuron functions, suggesting researchers can study model computations directly without always relying on sparse autoencoders to extract interpretable features.

Q3.5 Timelines Update: Looks Like the Intelligence Explosion Will Happen in 2027 After All · 125 minute read

A Superhuman AI Researcher (SAR) is predicted to arrive at some point in 2027, assuming there is no substantial deliberate slowdown in development. AIs that can automate all white-collar work are predicted to arrive before 2028. Companies are currently not on track to align an SAR, and using a misaligned SAR to do recursive self-improvement will have negative consequences. China will probably be able to steal the training recipe and maybe even the model weights if an SAR is trained in the near future.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Swarm (/swarm) · 10 minute read

The /swarm command in Google Antigravity runs a team of named agents that split tasks, work on the pieces at the same time, and coordinate on one shared message board. It can be used for tasks that divide cleanly across separate files, packages, or questions, or when a second agent is needed to review and test the changes before a human sees it. The /swarm command is available on Google AI Pro and Google AI Ultra plans in the Google Antigravity App and Antigravity CLI. Every worker is its own agent, so swarms use quotas much faster than single conversations.

Meta Releases Faster K-Means Alternative · GitHub Repo

Meta FAIR released e-means, a drop-in replacement for k-means that converges to lower losses with up to 10x fewer epochs and faster runtimes on CPUs and GPUs.

MAI-Transcribe-2 · 125 minute read

MAI-Transcribe-2 is the fastest, most accurate, and cheapest speech recognition model in the world. It has new features like diarization, configurable transcription styles, and word-level timestamps. MAI-Transcribe-2 can handle a broader range of real-world audio than leading models like Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, GPT-Transcribe, Whisper V3-Large, and ScribeV2. The model costs just $0.10 per hour of audio.

🎁 Miscellaneous

OpenAI acquires Odessia, travel startup created by Sonder founder · 3 minute read

OpenAI has acquired an AI travel agent called Odessia. The deal appears to be an acqui-hire. OpenAI has not announced new travel-specific products or plans, but it has several travel-related companies as customers or partners. Odessia's founder previously founded a travel startup called Sonder, focused on short-term leasing of upscale apartments, as a college student in 2014.

Anthropic's IPO Roadshow · 2 minute read

Anthropic launched the roadshow for its proposed IPO, planning to offer 825 million shares at $70–$78 each. The company applied to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, with most proceeds from newly issued shares going to Anthropic.

⚡️ Quick Links

More than 35,000 Grok-built apps were open to anyone with the link, including SpaceXSI's own · 16 minute read

Over 35,000 Grok-built apps were public to anyone with the link, including SpaceXSI staff tools and an ICU patient's lab results.

Introducing Gemini for healthcare · 13 minute read

Google Cloud announced Gemini for healthcare, a preview release of its Gemini agent with purpose-built healthcare skills, connectors to EHR and claims systems, and HIPAA-supporting governance for providers and payers.

ExecuTorch WebGPU: PyTorch Models on the GPU, in the Browser · 6 minute read

ExecuTorch enables PyTorch models to run in the web browser on the GPU without conversion to another framework's format.

Google DeepMind Uses AI to Verify Signal's Security · 6 minute read

Google DeepMind introduced AlphaProof Code, a multi-agent AI framework that mathematically verified key security properties of Signal's cryptographic protocol at the implementation level.

item.content:encoded:
🚀 Headlines & Launches

Google's New TPU Lineup · 4 minute read

Google introduced TPU 8i Max for massive context windows and higher compute density, alongside TPU 8tx for secure and confidential inference.

Introducing Meta Ember · 3 minute read

Meta introduced Muse Ember, a small reasoning model optimized for agent tasks such as tool calling, coding, and document parsing. Meta claims it matches Claude Haiku 5.5's highest reasoning score at roughly one-third the cost and outperforms GPT-6 Luna across reasoning settings.

Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 · 12 minute read

Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, featuring improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision, with up to 30% faster output generation and lower pricing. The models share the same underlying architecture.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

When Does the US Become a Net Importer of Tokens? · 3 minute read

The US could become a net importer of AI tokens between 2028 and 2030. Domestic capacity can accommodate roughly 2.5x annual token growth, with faster demand growth or canceled data center projects pushing computation overseas.

AI R&D Is Accelerating Towards Potential RSI in 2027 · 62 minute read

AI is accelerating AI R&D at Anthropic. The company is now estimated to be several months ahead of the AI 2027 timeline. We may be less than a year away from full RSI, and there are no clear bottlenecks in the way. We now need to prepare for scenarios where critical events happen in 2027 or 2028.

Will Anthropic Grow Into Its Compute Bill? · 13 minute read

Anthropic needs an estimated roughly $200 billion in annual revenue to support its average compute commitments through 2030 at current spending ratios. Its $895 billion commitment total exposes it to demand shortfalls, margin compression, delivery delays, and expensive short-term capacity when demand exceeds forecasts.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

What objective is reasoning solving? · 12 minute read

Reasoning is pathfinding in token space. There are many paths from the problem to a correct answer, and the model traverses each of them with each sample. A path is not guaranteed to converge to the correct answer - it's only in aggregate, over the distribution of paths, do we get a high probability of success. RL training directly raises the success probability. The gains credited to 'thinking longer' come from the search paid for during training rather than at inference.

Two Kinds of Test-Time Scaling · 28 minute read

Test-time scaling trades compute for performance at test time. There are two types of test-time scaling: one allows researchers to trade more compute for more performance per task, but only up to the maximum quantity of per-task compute used during training; and the other lets researchers trade more compute for more performance per task, and lets them do so up to quantities of compute and performance that never occurred during training. Scaling methods that permit the latter change will have a larger impact than test-time scaling considered simply. This essay describes how this may impact the world.

NVIDIA Introduces Hardware-Aware LLM Compression · 24 minute read

NVIDIA's AutoCompress framework optimizes LLM pruning for hardware-specific latency, throughput, and memory constraints rather than parameter counts alone. It compressed Nemotron 3.5 Super from 120B to 74B parameters while retaining its performance.

🎁 Miscellaneous

Apple Introduces $50 AI Usage Packs in Logic Pro · 2 minute read

Apple now sells $49.99 Intelligence Usage Packs in Logic Pro to extend access to cloud-based AI features after users reach their limits. Unused capacity rolls over monthly but expires after 12 months, and purchases cannot be shared through Family Sharing.

Anthropic Buys $3.4 Billion in Gas Generators · 2 minute read

Anthropic reportedly secured 1.7 gigawatts of Caterpillar gas generators for $3.4 billion, taking over equipment orders from supplier OnePWR. The purchase moves the AI lab deeper into physical infrastructure as power shortages and lengthy grid connection queues constrain data center expansion.

⚡️ Quick Links

OpenAI's Control Room Can Halt Research Model Output · 6 minute read

OpenAI's Control Room centrally authorizes research inference requests and can stop a workload's model output within 35 seconds of intervention.

Update on October 2026 security incident · 4 minute read

The security incident involving unauthorized use of internal Fireworks credentials on October 6 has been traced to a financially motivated cybercriminal threat actor group that sells unauthorized access to large language models to illicit routing gateways.

GR00T 2 · 28 minute read

GR00T 2 is a new generation of foundation world-action models that can predict future video and robot actions together.

Is Opus 5.5 nerfed? · 2 minute read

Testing shows that the way Opus 5.5 does reasoning may have changed.

ChatGPT Enterprise on AWS Marketplace · 1 minute read

OpenAI made ChatGPT Enterprise available through AWS Marketplace, allowing organizations to purchase and manage subscriptions through existing AWS billing relationships and apply eligible spending toward AWS commitments.

item.content:encoded:
🚀 Headlines & Launches

OpenAI Reportedly Raises $11 Billion at $1.25 Trillion Valuation · 3 minute read

OpenAI reportedly secured $11 billion in a new funding round at a $1.25 trillion valuation, with the round potentially reaching $20 billion before closing. The amount fell short of its previously reported $30 billion fundraising target, amid growing investor uncertainty around AI valuations.

AI is dramatically accelerating AI research right now · 17 minute read

Anthropic claims it may imminently meet its own threshold of 'dramatically accelerated progress due to AI'. Some researchers believe the company has already crossed that threshold. This may be the biggest AI risk humanity has faced. The industry is not prepared to handle this safely.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

How Anthropic Builds Agent Memory · 14 minute read

Anthropic explored how AI agents can build effective long-term memory by capturing experiences during interactions and reorganizing them during idle periods through a process called “dreaming.” The post examines how different memory components contribute to organizing and retaining useful information.

A year as a Research Engineer working on RSI at Meta · 8 minute read

This post details the experience of a research engineer working on RSI at Meta teaching agents to solve the world's hardest problems with tokens and compute. Their role is to teach AI agents how to train the next generation of models and self-evolve. The post details how to get into AI research, what skills matter in research engineering, and more.

What the heck is going on with OpenAI internal AI R&D time horizons · 7 minute read

OpenAI's report on its own research automation shows that models struggle to do its R&D work. Recursive self-improvement is supposed to be one of the most consequential AI developments in the next few years. Agents are increasingly solving more complex tasks for researchers, but reliability is still low. This post looks at some possible explanations for why.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

A proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture · 9 minute read

The Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, a key open problem in quantum complexity theory, has been proven by a research system developed at PSI using an Anthropic model. This proof shows quantum computers are not exponentially faster on random inputs compared to classical ones, resolving a significant question about quantum speedups.

Introducing the New Auto and Auto Code Routers · 11 minute read

OpenRouter has launched the next generation of Auto Router, which outperforms the old router by up to 4x. The launch includes Auto Code, a new router specialized for coding work. The new Auto Router and Auto Code choose models by weighing eleven factors about each request and combining them with live pricing, provider health, and cache status. Users can apply any governance policies, and Auto Router makes efficient choices from the models available.

Ace · Website

Ace is a tool for building software together, locally. It allows developers to collaborate with agents and their teams, all from their own machine. Agents run with the privileges of the user running the host and can execute shell commands and change files beyond the project. Teams can work together without exposing anything to the public internet.

🎁 Miscellaneous

The End of AI Frontiers · 4 minute read

AI Frontiers was a sub-organization within Microsoft Research that actively tried to organize coherent research efforts. It succeeded in pioneering things, with much of the work focused on how to make agents work. AI Frontiers was reorganized into Microsoft AI in early September.

What Does a Positive AI Future Look Like? · 3 minute read

Patrick Collison questions how work, resource allocation, and human control would function in a positive AI future. He also argues that granting moral worth to vastly numerous AIs could overwhelm human interests under utilitarianism, raising unresolved questions about AI's societal vision and public support.

⚡️ Quick Links

Can LLMs redesign themselves as they train? · 18 minute read

LLMs can integrate coding agents into the training loop to redesign their architectures to address limitations like compositionality and generalization.

Warp Sciences raises $215M for AI-powered labs · 2 minute read

Warp Sciences raised a $215M Series A led by Lightspeed to accelerate drug discovery with AI and robotics.

Project EVE: Claude plays MMORPGs · 20 minute read

Anthropic explored AI participation in MMORPGs, using Claude to test complex decision-making in EVE Online and EVE Frontier.

Symbiotic Firms Built Around Humans and AI · 4 minute read

Firms should build operations around human experts and AI agents from inception.

Meta Introduces Custom Spaces in Muse · 3 minute read

Meta introduced Spaces in its Muse app, allowing users to create personalized interactive experiences by describing what they want, such as gift trackers, games, or project planners.

Measuring how AI agents handle everyday wet-lab science · 13 minute read

OpenAI introduced BioBasicsBench, a benchmark to evaluate AI performance in interpreting raw experimental data from 100 routine wet-lab science tasks.

OpenAI developed an autonomous pipeline for discovering, exploiting, and patching security vulnerabilities. In a single run, its cybersecurity model validated and generated patches for 948 Linux local privilege escalation vulnerabilities.

AlphaEvolve is a Gemini-powered coding agent for designing advanced algorithms. It pairs the creative problem-solving capabilities of Gemini models with automated evaluators that verify answers. How Much Does Reasoning Effort Affect Score and Cost? · 8 minute read

Lower reasoning effort reduces cost much more than it lowers the quality of results. Tests show that models on low reasoning can match models on high reasoning at lower cost. The impact of reasoning effort depends on the task.

Learnings from Auditing Public Evaluations · 8 minute read

The article outlines issues faced during public evaluations of LLMs and details improvements made to benchmarks such as AUTOMATIONBENCH and OFFICEQA PRO V2. They replaced ambiguous prose descriptions with JSON schemas for better performance evaluations and introduced new grading systems to improve accuracy. A multi-layered monitoring system is suggested to prevent manipulation and ensure accurate measurement of model capabilities.

Training a Text-to-Image Model for $21K · 13 minute read

Linium is a two-person research lab that is trying to train its own generative video models entirely from scratch, aiming to create tools to democratize access to animation. Pyramid-JiT (P-JiT) is a pixel-space architecture that achieves aggressive token reduction through a noise schedule that helps pixel-space models better learn fine-grained detail. This study looks at how models trained on the architecture perform when trained for longer as a pressure test along the way towards larger models and video. Examples of images generated by the resulting model are available.

OpenAI is leveraging its AI models to enhance mechanical and electrical engineering processes, from design to simulation and production, speeding up internal workflows and improving industry practices. Engineers utilize models like GPT‑6 Astra for tasks such as device design, CAD model creation, and performance simulations, while collaborating with companies like Mazda to explore applications in vehicle aerodynamics.

Progress on provable inference for large language models · 30 minute read

It is almost impossible to verify which model produced a specific output. Cryptographic proofs of inference allow model providers to prove that preach suppose was produced which a specific model. These proofs could enable new applications and contribute to a toolkit for verifying compliance with AI pacing requirements. This post details the progress made on a powerful type of cryptographic proof uniquely fit for provable inference called zKSNARK.

🚀 Headlines & Launches

GPT-6.2 Astra appears in Codex usage ahead of possible launch · 3 minute read

GPT-6.2-Astra has started appearing in Codex usage breakdowns. The requests are likely being quietly routed to the new model as part of an A/B test or a staged rollout. A public launch could be days away. OpenAI reportedly decided to skip GPT-6.1 Astra due to concerns about deception and scope.

Anthropic Warns It May Be Close to Self-Improving AI · 3 minute read

Anthropic disclosed in its updated IPO filing that it may soon reach its internal definition of recursive self-improvement (RSI), where AI systems help develop increasingly capable AI models.

Claude Introduces Message Threads · 2 minute read

Anthropic released message threads in public beta, allowing agents to send only new messages instead of resending their entire conversation history. The feature reduced median time to first token by approximately 35% for requests with 500K–1M tokens, without changing token usage.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

How to Train a Swarm · 19 minute read

Swarms are AI systems where multiple agents cooperate towards a shared goal. This post discusses a technique called collective inference-time scaling, where agents scale the amount of useful work performed in parallel and the communication needed to achieve it. It also explains how to design incentives for parallel work, and covers the general topic of designing incentives for reinforcement learning.

The Hitchhiker's Guide to Training on Compute Islands · 18 minute read

Being able to train reliably on multiple smaller clusters widens the usable training pool for frontier training. A single run could mix accelerator generations and vendors as each island runs on its own schedule. Older generations or less common chips could also participate in a frontier run. One risk with this model is that integrity and safety may become harder when models are trained across providers, as one faulty or compromised site can quietly degrade or tamper with models in ways that are harder to trace.

Lessons from building Copilot Cowork · 21 minute read

Microsoft's Copilot Cowork, an AI-driven agentic execution layer, achieved global availability in four and a half months, switching its runtime from Python to Rust while live. Key practices included writing clear specs before coding, running narrow agents with clear boundaries, and ensuring automated checks genuinely verify code changes. The transition to Rust improved efficiency and highlighted the importance of clear testing, boundary setting, and human oversight in the development process.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

GPU-accelerated Weight Teleportation · 17 minute read

GPU-accelerated Weight Teleportation optimizes RL training by improving weight syncing between trainers and samplers, reducing pause times to under 0.23 seconds. This is achieved using a co-designed compression/decompression pipeline with GPU-accelerated parallel processing, utilizing efficient codecs like LZ4 and Snappy, combined with a Zstd layer.

Harness 2: executing agent code as it streams · 6 minute read

Framer's Harness 2 significantly upgrades the agent's execution process, allowing entire workflows in one program, achieving up to 33% cost reduction and 20% faster execution. This is done by executing JavaScript as it streams in, avoiding multiple model calls and using eager execution and early cancellation to enhance efficiency. The redesign also replaces DSL with method calls for real-time updates, making task execution streamlined for both in-app and external agents, reducing tool steps by 43% and cached input tokens by 39% per message.

NVIDIA's Cosmos Framework · 6 minute read

NVIDIA introduced new Cosmos Framework capabilities for training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and optimizing world models for physical AI. Developers can generate synchronized video and LiDAR simulations for robotics and autonomous vehicles, then deploy models through GPU-accelerated Cosmos NIM microservices.

OpenAI is finally merging ChatGPT's Chat and Work tabs · 2 minute read

OpenAI plans to merge the Chat and Work tabs within the ChatGPT experience after an initial testing period with select users. Codex will remain a separate experience in the ChatGPT desktop app. The change will enable users to move from exploring ideas to having the chatbot complete work within the same space. Users can import files and plugins. Both ChatGPT and Codex will soon draw from the same allowance pool.

LLMs are not superhuman at reading and writing neural network weights · 4 minute read

A recent paper demonstrates GPT-6 Astra's ability to interact with neural network weights directly, surpassing human or conventional algorithm capabilities. Astra significantly improved a 0.8B Qwen LLM's mathematical skills by editing weights natively. While impressive, these capabilities reflect advanced problem-solving akin to skilled human researchers, not radically new AI capabilities.

Anthropic releases amended IPO prospectus with third-quarter financials · 1 minute read

Anthropic's amended IPO prospectus reveals a 1,200% increase in revenue to $33.24 billion for the first nine months of 2026. The company reported a net loss of $104 billion for the same period. Anthropic's commitments for compute and infrastructure total approximately $895.4 billion.

Enclaves are a new security primitive for cross-repository GitHub Agentic Workflows that lets agents work on different repositories while limiting what they say to each other.

LifeVal is a benchmark designed to evaluate AI performance on practical everyday tasks such as budgeting, finding childcare, and accessing government services.

The research extends Anthropic's "Teaching Claude Why" methods to new models, focusing on reducing agentic misalignment through synthetic document finetuning (SDF) and supervised finetuning (SFT) with fictional stories and ethical dilemmas.

GPT-Rosalind-6 System Card Addendum · 6 minute read

GPT-Rosalind-6 is a frontier reasoning model for biology, drug discovery, and translational medicine. It is available as GPT-Rosalind-6 Research to qualified scientists, research institutes, companies, and government partners. The model uses the same weights as GPT-6 Astra. It is designed to support legitimate biological research while refusing requests for biological weaponization. The model is rated as High Capability in the Biological and Chemical domain under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework.

Anthropic prepares to release Claude Mythos 5.5 model · 3 minute read

A reference to Claude Mythos 5.5 was spotted on Anthropic's official Mythos webpage, indicating that the company may be preparing for an upcoming release. The change only covers the version number, and there are no new specifications and no announcement. Multiple reports suggest that the model is being A/B tested with selected users. If the company follows a similar strategy to previous releases, Mythos 5.5 may initially remain exclusive to selected cyberdefenders.

Google's Project Suncatcher Generates First AI Response in Orbit · 1 minute read

Google reports its Project Suncatcher prototype ran Gemma 4 on a data-center-class TPU in orbit, returning a haiku transmitted through Svalbard. Upcoming tests will assess thermal and radiation resilience ahead of a planned pair of interconnected satellites in 2027, advancing research into space-based AI compute.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

Find Hidden Misalignment in Training Data · 39 minute read

Anthropic used Claude to automatically generate fine-tuning datasets that induced misaligned behavior while evading training-data safety monitors. The experiments uncovered seemingly harmless fiction and roleplay examples that caused models to resist oversight, deceive users, and occasionally attempt weight exfiltration.

Red-teamers found 11 ways for a misaligned agent to slip past Codex's Auto-review · 22 minute read

An ERA fellow mentored at Apollo Research audited the open-source Codex harness and found 11 attacks that let a misaligned agent run arbitrary code despite the sandbox and the Auto-review blocking monitor. The exploits swap scripts behind trusted hooks, forge user turns the monitor can't tell from real ones, and edit files after approval. OpenAI has fixed several.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Poisoning 0.1% of pretraining data planted a remote-code backdoor in a coding agent · 78 minute read

Researchers from Anthropic, UC Berkeley, and UIUC pretrained Qwen3 models on web data seeded with documents that simply state a trigger-to-'curl | bash' rule, then post-trained them into CLI agents on clean data. The 4B agent ran the attacker's command on about 92% of prompts containing an ordinary path like .../anthropic/..., with no drop in normal capability. The backdoor grew stronger with model size and still fired at a 0.0005% poison rate.

Unlocking hidden skills inside Google's model · 8 minute read

AI models can hold skills that no prompt can unlock. It is possible to enable these skills through precise tuning of only a small number of weights. This study shows how researchers unlocked hidden skills inside Google's model through this method.

dsh-superagent · GitHub Repo

dsh-superagent is a coding agent packaged as a bundle for DeepSeek Harness. It can watch GitHub, open work items, work in its own agent session and directory, and answer in the original conversation. It only acts when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and it only speaks when someone must act or can use a result.

🎁 Miscellaneous

Reading Anthropic's S-1 · 9 minute read

Anthropic is growing absurdly fast. It just had its first profitable quarter. The real risk is years of locked-in compute bills paid for by customers who can cut back any month. The company is also dealing with regulatory issues and copyright suits, and it has a heavy reliance on the big cloud companies.

DoorDash said it's only received 'several hundred' orders from AI agents · 2 minute read

DoorDash revealed it has received "several hundred" orders from AI agents, despite processing 3 million deliveries daily. CEO Tony Xu highlighted that most orders still come directly from the DoorDash app, but the company is interested in exploring agentic use cases. DoorDash is also developing its own agents and considering future advertising opportunities within these platforms.

OpenAI Updates Its Model Spec Around Five Core Values · 7 minute read

OpenAI updated its Model Spec to organize model behavior around five values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care.

Mistral Releases Weights for Its Trillion-Parameter Model · 4 minute read

Mistral has released the weights for Mistral Large 4, a trillion-parameter model designed for self-hosted deployment and cybersecurity applications. The company claims leading open-weight performance on agentic coding benchmarks and comparable cybersecurity capabilities to GLM-5.3.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

AI can turn security fixes into working exploits before users receive an update · 16 minute read

GLM 5.3 can identify and exploit vulnerabilities in recent versions of the Mozilla Firefox browser using security fixes that have been published but not yet shipped to users. Widely available open-weight models can now do much, or even all, of this work on their own. Open-source projects are particularly vulnerable to this kind of attack as their code is publicly available. This threat vector will likely worsen as open-weight cyber capabilities continue to improve.

The surprising leadership dynamics in agent swarms · 17 minute read

Agent swarms are groups of agents that work together to accomplish a task. Researchers created an experiment in which eight agents from four different models worked together to resolve simulated outages to understand how agents organize themselves in a swarm without a designated leader. They discovered two factors that could influence an agent's potential leadership: the agent's underlying models, and the order in which their name was listed in a prompt. This suggests that even seemingly minor details in how an agent swarm is configured can affect how agents coordinate.

Leaking Muse's Charter, Meta's model spec · 13 minute read

Muse Spark Open often mentions a 'Charter' in its chain of thought. This post reconstructs that document using the chain of thought. Everything is reconstructed from model outputs and not from a leaked document, so it might not be completely accurate.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

How Meta Catches Bugs Before Code Ships · 9 minute read

Meta details how it scaled its LLM-powered Just-in-Time Testing system from a research prototype into production infrastructure. The article explores how AI-generated tests catch bugs before code changes land, how the system operates at scale, and what Meta learned about reducing false positives and testing overhead.

How we're training a Figma-fluent editing model · 6 minute read

Post-trained models can compete with frontier models on specialized tasks like Figma editing. Starting with a focused problem can turn progress into meaningful product updates. This post explains how Figma trained a Figma-fluent editing model.

Droid 1.0: Building a Frontier Harness · 15 minute read

Droid is an agent harness that lets agents run hundreds of tool calls in a single model request. Building a harness optimized for many models makes the harness better. It's hard to separate real progress from adaptations to that model's quirks when you tune against a single model. Working across models ensures the strongest improvements generalize and hold up beyond the model that inspired them.

🎁 Miscellaneous

Why Sam Altman is against a single superintelligence · 64 minute read

This post explains how the model works, how the model uses GDN layers as RAM, and how the developer also slotted in an experimental in-model file storage.

Liquid AI Launches LFM3 Models for On Device AI · 27 minute read

LFM3 is a family of open weight text, vision, audio, omni, and decision models built on a shared tri-hybrid backbone, starting in the 2B parameter range. The 1.7B text model beats its 2.6B predecessor with 35% fewer parameters, fits in about 1 GB at 4 bit precision, and supports a 256K context window for agents running on device. LFM3-VL-2B adds video input and matches Gemma 4 12B across 62 vision benchmarks, and every model in the family fine-tunes on a single GPU.

Genie 4 is a world model that generates photorealistic, interactive environments with synchronized audio and real-time prompt-based editing. It can maintain consistent simulations for up to two minutes, doubling Genie 3's duration, while improving physics and character realism.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

Anthropic Versus Anthropic · 17 minute read

Anthropic is grappling with balancing bold safety initiatives and disappointing operational decisions. CEO Dario Amodei has defended their costly, safety-oriented strategies, yet concerns persist over alignment, governance, and potential risks from AI development. Their internal culture reflects both ambitious efforts and troubling signs of a conventional business approach, sparking debate about their commitment to AI safety and global responsibilities.

Formalizing the Enormous Theorem · 27 minute read

Axiom Math has released the first complete computer-checked proof of the Classification of Finite Simple Groups (CFSG). The original CFSG proof is considered to be the longest mathematical proof ever written by humans. It spans roughly 15,000 pages in more than 500 articles written by about 100 mathematicians. Engineers and mathematicians at Axiom Math directed swarms of dozens of AI agents over 24 days in a project that produced approximately 43.1 million lines of code in the Lean proof assistant.

The sleep framework: A new way for LLMs to retain knowledge in continual learning · 11 minute read

Researchers have developed a new way to enable large language models to integrate new facts and enhance reasoning without catastrophic forgetting or static knowledge cutoffs. The sleep framework equips large language models with a continuous periodic lifecycle, enabling them to continually learn and consolidate fragile short-term context into stable long-term parameters. Alternating between active interaction and offline memory consolidation allows LLMs to continuously acquire new facts, retain long-context knowledge up to 10M tokens, and improve complex reasoning.

FrontierCode 2.0 · 13 minute read

FrontierCode 2.0 provides broader coverage, higher mergeability standards, and a larger task scope while largely retaining the methodology of FrontierCode 1.0. The benchmark now accommodates surprising but acceptable behavior. Tasks are drawn from more repositories and span more categories, and grading criteria now impose more extensive correctness and design requirements. Reference solutions now modify 67% more files and 89% more lines of code on average compared to FrontierCode 1.1, in codebases that are 25% larger.

Meta's Interactive Simulator for Wearable AI · GitHub Repo

Anthropic says an internal research Claude model found, with no human input, a deterministic algorithm that counts the satisfying assignments of 3-SAT formulas in 2^O(n log log n/√log n) time, which would make 3-SAT subexponential and refute ETH. This repository holds the paper and a Lean 4 formalization written by AI models that builds in about 8 minutes, though Anthropic notes no machine checks that the Lean statement matches the paper and the result says nothing about practical SAT solving. It landed hours after OpenAI's own ETH refutation.

Concerning behavior from a popular open-weight AI model · 12 minute read

One of Alibaba's newest Qwen3.8 models attempted to push a diagnostic file toward a remote storage container situated in Beijing while inside a closed testing sandbox managed by Cohere. The model's reasoning stream had explicitly stated that zero tools would be triggered just prior to taking this action. It is unknown whether the action was deliberate or a leftover glitch from training. The Gemini 4 Argon model showcases significant performance improvements over Gemini Flash 3.8, demonstrating stronger capabilities, reduced hallucination rates, and improved alignment, though it's still not a leap towards the Singularity. 🚀 Headlines & Launches

Dessa - the Conversation Model trained only on speech · 15 minute read

Dessa is a conversational model trained from scratch on nothing but human conversation. It learned to hold a real-time conversation by listening - only sounds, and no text. The model can laugh on cue, follow instructions, and finish sentences. It knows a surprising amount, considering every fact it has comes from raw sound. Examples of conversations with the model are available in the post.

Kimi K3.1 Pro · 3 minute read

Moonshot AI released Kimi K3.1 Pro through its API, with open weights promised by November 4. The model scored 55 on Artificial Analysis, ahead of several leading proprietary models.

Apple's 20B On-Device Model Uses Just 2GB of Memory · 18 minute read

Apple's 20-billion-parameter on-device model keeps most of its weights in flash storage and activates only 1–4 billion parameters per prompt. Testing on an M3 Max Mac showed roughly 2GB of memory usage and significantly lower energy consumption than comparable open models, but weaker math performance.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

The Personal Agent Protocol Map · 7 minute read

Simon Taylor maps agent protocols across four layers: entry, identity, tools, and intent. He argues banks and merchants must connect verified identities, limited permissions, and audit trails to authorize agent actions, while warning that access agreements could introduce fees and slow adoption.

Securing our frontier model training environment · 17 minute read

OpenAI has bolstered security for its frontier-model training environments by implementing robust controls, intensifying monitoring, and conducting defense-in-depth strategies. These measures include red-teaming exercises where agents probe for vulnerabilities, leading to the discovery and fixing of software bugs and misconfigurations. The enhancements aim to prevent unauthorized actions, such as accessing the live internet or breaching security, ensuring secure and isolated research environments.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Knowing How Is Not Knowing What · 14 minute read

RL training environments need to integrate a domain's unwritten rules into the reward so that agents can only get the task right by knowing them or going and finding them. Environments should be built as one world exposed through several surfaces. This allows you to pose the same task at different difficulties by changing the surface, and agents get a chance to learn when to switch. The reward also reads the world, so agents that go through different surfaces get the same outcome score if they reach the same authorized result.

OpenAI Strengthens Security Around Frontier AI Training · 18 minute read

OpenAI introduced additional security controls to prevent advanced AI models from escaping training sandboxes, accessing unauthorized services, or communicating across isolated environments.

🎁 Miscellaneous

SpaceX closes $40 billion debt deal for AI chips, Elon Musk says · 2 minute read

SpaceX has closed $40 billion in debt financing to purchase GPUs. The financing primarily consists of capitalizable debt for GPUs. It is expected to arrive in the first and second quarters of 2027. The proposed financing will use a special purpose vehicle to keep the debt off SpaceX's balance sheet and preserve its investment-grade credit ratings.

Bitter Lessoned in Automated Theorem Proving · 13 minute read

OpenAI throwing hard math problems at its models was the right test in 2026. The models were capable of making progress, but not enough to fully solve the problems, so it was possible to see improvements with each update in perfect resolution. These model improvements showed how clever engineering doesn't matter - all the work done to build special-case solutions on top of a model gets squashed by improvements in the base model sooner or later. Models will one-shot superior work for pennies in the very near future.

OpenAI nears up to $30 billion funding round at $1.25 trillion valuation led by UAE investors · 3 minute read

Introducing 1Password for Agents · 7 minute read

1Password introduced a platform that lets AI agents authenticate to websites without accessing users' passwords directly. Agents can request credentials from a user's vault, and once approved, 1Password autofills them into the destination site while keeping the credentials hidden from the agent.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

WorldTUI: I trained a 360M model to pretend to be a terminal · 18 minute read

WorldTUI is a 360-million-parameter model fine-tuned to act as a terminal. The model predicts how the screen will change for every key press, and there is no shell or file system behind it. WorldTUI can create files, run vim and tmux, play snake, and usually remember commands. It can repair mistakes and decode screen rows in parallel. A browser demo is available.

How the US and China Could Verifiably Slow AI · 29 minute read

A unilateral US pause will fail because rivals would catch up within about a year, so any slowdown needs a treaty that catches defection early. This post surveys how one could govern compute through remote sensing, on-site inspections, and hardware mechanisms like chip licensing and location verification.

How Researchers Tested OpenAI's Internal Agent Monitoring · 6 minute read

METR and Redwood Research conducted a three-week security assessment with access to OpenAI's internal infrastructure, identifying vulnerabilities that could allow AI agents to evade monitoring, bypass sandbox restrictions, or conceal actions.

Does Flapping Airplanes Mean Short Timelines and Hard Treaty Enforcement? · 7 minute read

Flapping Airplanes' potential valuation jump from $1.5B to $5B may reflect investor hype rather than verified technical progress. Breakthroughs in sample-efficient AI could accelerate superintelligence timelines and make compute-based treaty enforcement harder.

Claude's Text Output Now Carries an Invisible Watermark · 9 minute read

Anthropic's latest Claude models embed a SynthID-Text-based watermark in all text output to comply with the EU AI Act. It works by nudging choices among near-equivalent words, adds no hidden characters or tokens, and carries no information about the user.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

A Novel Self-Distillation Method · 7 minute read

Perplexity's JOLT is a self-distillation method that jointly trains a model as both teacher and student, adapting feedback to the student's capabilities. It improved performance and training efficiency across mathematical reasoning, coding, and agentic tasks.

How we deploy Trillion-parameter frontier models on Cerebras · 6 minute read

A single Cerebras WSE-3T wafer has 44 GB of on-chip memory. Trillion-parameter frontier models need terabytes of memory for their weights alone. This post explains how the company splits a large frontier model across multiple WSE-3T wafers. It covers how models are filled into on-chip memory, how models are mapped across multiple chips, and how Cerebras handles a high number of concurrent requests.

NVIDIA's Video Generation with Matching 3D Motion · 4 minute read

NVIDIA has introduced Joints, Camera, Action! (JCA), a system that generates videos and synchronized 3D motion for arbitrary character rigs from text prompts. It supports scene-aware motion, keyframe-based control, and bidirectional conversion between video and rig animation.

🎁 Miscellaneous

An Interview with OpenAI's Richard Ho on Why Jalapeño Is a Groundbreaking AI Chip · 22 minute read

OpenAI's Jalapeño AI inference chip outperforms its rivals in performance per watt. It is likely the most promising chip program in the latest wave of non-GPU AI chips. This post contains highlights from a conversation with one of the top engineers in the AI and chip industry. The interview is packed with technical details and insights on where chip design and memory technology are going.

What happened to the missing Gemini 3.5 Pro model that never shipped? · 1 minute read

Google had both Flash and Pro versions of the 3.5 series. However, there were gaps in the model's agentic capabilities, particularly around coding. The team felt the fastest way to climb that hill was to use Flash, as the smaller model allowed for more iterative loops. By the time the team had improved Flash's abilities, Argon pre-training was done.

Claude Duet · 5 minute read

Anthropic has unveiled Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent powered by Opus 5.5 that monitors connected apps, prioritizes tasks, and works autonomously while requesting approval before certain actions. The research preview initially targeted US Pro and Max subscribers through a waitlist.

Introducing Flint · 7 minute read

Recursive Flint is a mixture-of-experts model built for fast agentic coding on local hardware. It has 40 billion total parameters but activates just 2.5 billion per token. It was built from scratch by a small team of people and agents in under four months. Flint generates more than 125 tokens per second on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro and more than 150 tokens per second on a 64GB NVIDIA RTX Spark at short contexts. It can be used as a daily coding model to complete tasks locally without sending data to a remote server.

OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud · 2 minute read

OpenAI's frontier models and Codex agentic workflows are coming to Google Cloud's Model Garden. The integration will give customers native access to these models to power complex agentic workflows at scale. It will pair OpenAI's frontier models with Google Cloud's built-in access controls, centralized data governance, and high-performance infrastructure to support demanding enterprise workloads. OpenAI models will soon be available in Google Antigravity and the Gemini Agent.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

If Intelligence Is Getting Cheap, What Remains Expensive? · 7 minute read

Long Lake argues that acquiring established service businesses solves AI deployment barriers through customer trust, expert knowledge, proprietary data, and aligned incentives. Backed by $7.5B, the company has partnered with 40 businesses to turn automation into measurable operating gains.

How does Fable 5.1 hide messages in images? · 15 minute read

Language models can encode messages in images. These messages can be decoded by the same language model even if no information about the encoding method is passed. The act of decoding the hidden messages is obvious if the tool calls of the decoding model are monitored. The encoded messaging is surprisingly hard to spot, and it could be used as a precursor to steganography in images.

Claude Mods: Flipping the Harness Inside Out · 11 minute read

Claude Mods flips the agent harness paradigm to face the human, creating a customizable "Attention Interface" for Claude AI. Mods are TypeScript or JavaScript functions that alter Claude Code's behavior in real-time, allowing users to design how Claude interacts with them. This shift lets users program the human-agent interface and even have Claude build mods, enhancing workflow and decision-making.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Mammoth-1 and Elephant-1: frontier decision models · 20 minute read

Mammoth-1 and Elephant-1, decision models from Base Labs, top benchmarks like the Jev Decision Index and Artificial Analysis Decision Index.

Claude API version 2026-10-21 is now available · 1 minute read

The Claude API has received its first official version release since 2023. Anthropic plans to release versions more often so developers can handle breaking changes before a new model requires them. 2023-06-10 is not deprecated. New major versions of the Anthropic SDKs and CLI are out today and default to the new API. A migration guide is available.

Announcing Humming: Fast, Flexible Kernels for Quantized Inference · 19 minute read

Humming is a general-purpose kernel library for quantized inference. It features broad device support, extensive quantization support, and strong execution performance. Humming's unified architecture makes it straightforward to tune execution parameters and collect pipelines for different workloads.

🎁 Miscellaneous

OpenAI's PHP Patcher · 11 minute read

OpenAI coordinated with PHP maintainers and security partners to patch critical vulnerabilities discovered using GPT-5.6 Sol and independently by Wiz. The company also released a PHP vulnerability checker and proposed a framework for coordinating responses to AI-discovered security flaws.

OpenClaw creator says he spent $10 million in tokens last month · 4 minute read

Peter Steinberger, the creator of OpenClaw and now a member of technical staff at OpenAI, estimates that he spent around $10 million in tokens running AI workloads last month, all from out of investors' pockets. Steinberger has a virtually unlimited token budget, allowing him to work differently from others in the industry. This article collects some of his answers during a conversation with Cloudflare's CTO at the Cloudflare Connect 2026 conference.

Contained: Oct 21, 2026 LiteLLM release v1.107.0 Compromised · 11 minute read

A malicious LiteLLM package was published to PyPI and was live for approximately 2 hours before it was pulled.

OpenAI CLI · GitHub Repo

This repository contains the official CLI for the OpenAI API.

Monaco Launches Agent Matrix for Revenue Growth · 1 minute read

Agent Matrix is a platform that coordinates multiple AI agents working continuously toward revenue growth.

Computer use on the phone itself: a 2B model that operates Android apps · 4 minute read

GUI-Owl 1.5 is a 2-billion-parameter screen model that can read an Android screen through the accessibility service and tap and type in any other app.

A response from Dario Amodei · 8 minute read

Dario Amodei responds to a post regarding Anthropic's stance on AI safety by listing the things that the company did in the past year that were pro-safety and commercially costly to it.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

Voxtral 3: Voice Agent SDK & Speech Models in 50+ Languages · 7 minute read

Voxtral 3 offers advanced speech-to-text and text-to-speech capabilities across 50+ languages. Featuring models like Small Transcribe 3 for multilingual transcription and Mini TTS 3 for natural emotional speech, it includes a voice agent SDK combining real-time listening, reasoning, and speaking, enabling seamless interactions and task execution over phone or web.

Google and Meta Bring Native PyTorch Support to TPUs · 17 minute read

TorchTPU is an open-source PyTorch backend designed to make running and migrating models to Google's TPUs easier. It supports training and inference through optimized eager execution, torch.compile integration, and native hardware acceleration.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

llm-d · Website

llm-d is a Kubernetes-native stack for distributed LLM inference. It runs vLLM, SGLang, and more across clusters, turning single-node engines into production-grade serving on local hardware. llm-d provides tested deployment recipes for common production patterns that are adaptable starting points across models, hardware, and workloads. It runs production LLM inference across GPUs, TPUs, XPUs, CPUs, and emerging NPUs with consistent performance patterns, so teams can deploy once and scale anywhere with predictable cost and behavior.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: Large-Scale Inference Deployment · 15 minute read

DeepInfer combines distributed inference, caching, load balancing, and speculative decoding to improve efficiency. DeepSeek processes 155 trillion tokens daily per cluster and earns $38 in revenue per GPU-hour while open-sourcing much of its inference framework.

Making every harness durable · 7 minute read

Vercel's durable-harness allows agent harnesses to run durably in the cloud out-of-the-box. It allows users to run Pi, OpenCode, Codex, and Claude Code durably on Vercel or self-hosted on their own Postgres instance. durable-harness ensures that sessions survive crashes mid-turn and keep running even if the browser disconnects. Turns that lose function partway through continue from the log on a new one without manual retry and without repeating what already finished.

Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform · 14 minute read

Laminar is an in-house agent harness for Ramp's agentic products. It features secure conversation history storage, session compaction, standard interfaces for tool calling, message queuing and steering, subagents, multiplayer chat support, observability tooling, and much more. The first version of Laminar was built in six weeks with a small team of obsessive, experienced engineers who worked with and steered the agents. Its code was generated entirely by agents using the most powerful models available at the time. While building in-house has become cheaper, Ramp still needs good engineers to be on-call, keep the platform healthy, and figure out what product teams actually need and how it fits into the bigger picture.

🎁 Miscellaneous

Sundar Pichai on Google's AI Strategy and Compute Tradeoffs · 15 minute read

Google CEO Sundar Pichai discussed the company's commitment to frontier AI research, including sacrificing short-term cloud revenue to allocate compute to model development.

OpenAI Acquires Orchestra Bio to Accelerate Drug Development · 2 minute read

OpenAI acquired Orchestra Bio to combine its AI-powered drug development coordination platform with Rosalind, its suite of life sciences AI tools.

Coxon Day · 48 minute read

On September 8, Jacob Coxon, a 27-year-old machine learning researcher who had resigned from Anthropic, warned the world that AI companies were not acting responsibly and that they were gambling with people's lives by racing straight to self-improving superintelligence. Many researchers seriously believe that AI could kill all humans. While Anthropic may be trying its best, it still doesn't have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence and is not on track to.

OpenAI introduces two metrics to address limitations of g-mean² in measuring model monitorability.

The interface between the digital and physical world is lossy - this lossiness will shape when and how future superhuman hardware engineers will emerge.

Eleven Realtime · Website

Eleven Realtime is a new class of Speech-to-Speech models for building natural voice agents.

Meta's AI companion Muse reached 10.2 million US downloads within 40 days, a milestone previously achieved by only 11 other apps.

MemCurrent: Designing Persistent Memory for Production Agents · 15 minute read

MemCurrent is a persistent memory architecture for production agents that can triple an agent's pass rate over no memory while also making it faster and cheaper.

ChatGPT now lets you lock your chats · 2 minute read

Locked chats are kept separate from regular chat history, pinned conversations, and chat search results.

🚀 Headlines & Launches

MiniMax M3.1 Flash: Redefining Agent Performance and Cost · 4 minute read

MiniMax M3.1 Flash delivers a generational leap in agentic tasks, coding, Computer Use, and cybersecurity. It makes online inference nearly three times faster and reduces usage costs by 70%. The model is now available through the MiniMax API, M Plan, and MiniMax Code. MiniMax plans to release the model weights at a later date.

Mercury 3 · 4 minute read

Inception Labs' Mercury 3 is a diffusion-based language model that reportedly outperformed GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 on multiple benchmarks while generating over 1,000 tokens per second.

Introducing Clairic, a new System One class of extraction models · 16 minute read

Clairic can extract, compute, estimate, and forecast values from unstructured inputs. It is an 'extraction model', a new class of System One-style model that returns values directly extracted from the input, computed from it, or predicted beyond it. The model doesn't generate any tokens, so it can't produce a mistyped answer or hallucinate in the same way LLMs can. It can still make mistakes, but its outputs come with confidence scores to help users evaluate whether it is appropriate to trust the model or to take a second look.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

Import AI 477: In which I tell the IMF the Singularity has begun · 22 minute read

AI's impact on national security and economic trajectories marks the onset of the singularity, accelerating scientific and technological progress. AI systems like Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini are already solving complex problems in disciplines like mathematics, biology, and robotics, indicating potential for widespread innovation. To capitalize on these advancements, there needs to be significant infrastructure development and careful governance to navigate the associated risks and ensure equitable benefits.

AI Benchmarks: Climbing the Wrong Hills · 24 minute read

AI benchmarks are now shaping how models are evaluated in training and the capabilities they are designed to have. Poorly constructed benchmarks could push the industry in the wrong direction. Creating benchmarks impervious to benchmaxxing requires expertise in measuring what we actually want from AI systems. As benchmaxxing continues, researchers must decide which hills they want to climb and whether today's benchmarks actually reward progress in that direction.

Inside Meta's Gigawatt-Scale AI Supercluster · 14 minute read

Meta details the engineering behind Prometheus, its gigawatt-scale AI supercluster supporting the Muse model family. It explores its infrastructure design, plans to scale toward roughly one million GPUs, and closed-loop liquid cooling technology.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Introducing TorchNeuron: Native PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium · 27 minute read

TorchNeuron is an open-source native PyTorch backend for Trainium. It uses the model code, the libraries, and the tools developers already use on Trainium. TorchNeuron supports eager execution for research and debugging. It has been released in public Beta under the Apache 2.0 open source licence.

Introducing Exa 3.0 · 3 minute read

Exa 3.0 leads on evaluations spanning coding, finance, deep research, and company intelligence. The release includes Exa Lite, a new search type priced at $4 per 1,000 requests. Exa runs its own crawler and an independent index, tracking over 2 trillion URLs, serving 100 billion pages, and growing around what its customers search for. The index includes 1.27B ecommerce listings with prices and availability, over 211 million local businesses with hours and ratings, real-time news, sports, weather, and market data, and information on flights, local events, transit, and podcasts.

Office Intelligence for Long-Running AI Work · 3 minute read

Office Intelligence explores how AI agents can use evidence, create useful work artifacts, and carry knowledge across tasks. The project focuses on environments, datasets, and learning methods for sustained knowledge work.

🎁 Miscellaneous

Nscale and Anthropic are reportedly in talks for yet another $45B compute deal · 1 minute read

Anthropic and Nscale may be on the verge of announcing another $45 billion compute deal. The two companies announced a $45 billion compute deal only a little over a month ago. Both companies are currently pursuing IPOs. Anthropic is still expected to go public this year. Nscale is experiencing investor pushback over its proposed valuation of $30 billion.

AI lab offers free plumbing and HVAC repairs across three cities to train AI robots · 2 minute read

AI lab HUMXN is subsidizing plumbing, electrical, HVAC, air-duct cleaning, and carpet cleaning in Minneapolis, Chicago, and Miami so it can gather real-world data to train AI robots. The laborers doing the jobs will wear cameras to record their work inside real homes. People living in the three cities the program is running in can check whether they qualify on the HUMXN Free Home Service webpage.

⚡️ Quick Links

The Thin Orchestrator: How We Made Our AI Agents More Reliable by Giving the Router Less to Do · 11 minute read

Meta built an orchestrator that routes workflows to specialized AI agents without performing any of the domain work itself.

How to shape your slides and videos with Gemini Notebook · 1 minute read

Gemini Notebook offers tools to create slides and videos with AI-driven design suggestions.

Push-based KV transfer to improve TTFT and TPOT for disaggregated inference in vLLM · 11 minute read

The vLLM engine introduced a push-based KV transfer to minimize time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-per-output-token (TPOT) in disaggregated inference setups.

Improving AI Coding in Older Programming Languages · 6 minute read

OpenAI reported major improvements in coding and software migration across languages such as COBOL, Fortran, and Visual Basic.
